# MBS scenario, Stage 1: facts note

*Generated by `compute.py` from tracked data, cut at 2025-12-31. Do not edit by hand. Advisor note (Nicholas Beroud);
descriptive, not a scored result.*

"MBS" below means the Fed's agency securities in total: the caps and the reinvestment rules apply to agency debt and
agency MBS together, and agency debt is about \$2.3bn, too small to change any figure here.

## 1. Policy timeline

| Date | What the Fed decided (MBS) | Why it matters for reserves | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14 Jun 2017 | First MBS runoff cap: \$4bn a month, rising by \$4bn every three months to \$20bn. | Runoff, not sales: the pace is set by homeowners' paydowns, up to the cap. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20170614c.htm) |
| 20 Mar 2019 | From Oct 2019, MBS paydowns up to \$20bn a month go into Treasuries; the aim is to hold "primarily Treasury securities in the longer run". | The Fed's stated preference for an all-Treasury balance sheet, the origin of the MBS problem. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20190320c.htm) |
| 31 Jul 2019 | Runoff ends in August, two months early. | Reserve drain stops; MBS keeps shrinking as paydowns move into Treasuries (reserve-neutral). | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20190731a.htm) |
| 15 Mar 2020 | Buy "at least \$200 billion" of agency MBS; reinvest all paydowns in MBS. | QE begins: MBS purchases add reserves. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20200315a.htm) |
| 23 Mar 2020 | Buy MBS "in the amounts needed". | Open-ended purchases; the holdings build that QT2 later works against. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20200323a.htm) |
| 16 Dec 2020 | "At least \$40 billion per month" of agency MBS. | The steady QE pace through 2021. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20201216a.htm) |
| 3 Nov 2021 | Taper: MBS purchases cut by \$5bn a month. | Reserve injection starts to slow. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20211103a.htm) |
| 15 Dec 2021 | Taper doubled: MBS purchases cut by \$10bn a month. | Faster end to purchases. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20211215a.htm) |
| 26 Jan 2022 | Net purchases end "in early March". | Holdings peak shortly after. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20220126a.htm) |
| 4 May 2022 | QT2: MBS cap \$17.5bn a month from June, \$35bn from September. | Runoff resumes; the cap is the most the Fed will let mature without reinvesting. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20220504b.htm) |
| 1 May 2024 | MBS cap stays \$35bn; paydowns above it go into Treasuries (from June). | Irrelevant in practice: paydowns never reached \$35bn (see below). | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20240501a1.htm) |
| 19 Mar 2025 | MBS cap stays \$35bn (Treasury cap cut to \$5bn from April). | The MBS drain continues while the Treasury drain nearly stops. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20250319a1.htm) |
| 29 Oct 2025 | Runoff ends 1 Dec; "reinvest all principal payments ... of agency securities into Treasury bills". | From December, MBS paydowns no longer drain reserves: a shift from MBS to bills. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20251029a1.htm) |
| 10 Dec 2025 | Reinvestment into bills repeated; reserve-management bill purchases begin. | The Fed now adds reserves on purpose; any MBS scenario is measured against that. | [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20251210a1.htm) |

All of these are linked from the Fed's [Policy Normalization page](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/policy-normalization.htm).
Caps and effective dates match this repository's `tests/fixtures/snapshots/fomc_notes/runoff_caps.csv`.

Peak: **\$2.74tn** in the week ended 2022-04-13, after QE.

## 3. Rules vs reality

Monthly change in holdings (from H.4.1 week-average first prints), against the cap in force and the 30-year
mortgage rate (Freddie Mac, via FRED):

| Regime | Months | Average monthly reduction | Largest month | Average cap | Months at the cap | Average mortgage rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QT1: passive runoff under a cap | 2017-10 to 2019-07 (19) | \$13.7bn | \$28.2bn | \$16.2bn | 8 of 19 | 4.39% |
| Paydowns into Treasuries (up to \$20bn a month) | 2019-08 to 2020-02 (7) | \$19.0bn | \$30.8bn | none | 0 of 7 | 3.63% |
| QE: net purchases | 2020-03 to 2022-03 (25) | −\$53.6bn | \$7.4bn | none | 0 of 25 | 3.08% |
| All paydowns reinvested in MBS | 2022-04 to 2022-05 (2) | −\$4.5bn | \$1.9bn | none | 0 of 2 | 5.11% |
| QT2: passive runoff under a cap | 2022-06 to 2025-11 (42) | \$15.8bn | \$28.7bn | \$33.8bn | 1 of 42 | 6.61% |
| All paydowns into Treasury bills | 2025-12 to 2025-12 (1) | \$22.2bn | \$22.2bn | none | 0 of 1 | 6.19% |

A negative reduction is growth (QE purchases). Single months are noisy: MBS purchases and reinvestments settle
on fixed monthly dates, so one month can swing well above or below the cap and the next swing back. Read the
averages; the "months at the cap" count is indicative only.

## 4. What the facts show

1. **The \$35bn cap never bound.** From Sep 2022 to Nov 2025 the reduction averaged **\$16.6bn a month**,
   at most \$28.7bn (2022-11), and reached the cap in 0 of 39 months. The cap
   was a ceiling the market never tested; the realized pace is the measure that matters.
2. **Mortgage rates set the pace.** Over QT2 the 30-year rate averaged 6.61% (range
   4.99% on 2022-08-04 to 7.79% on 2023-10-26; at or above 7% in
   26 of 183 weeks), and holdings fell about 0.70% a month. From Aug 2019 to
   Feb 2020, with the rate around 3.63%, they fell about 1.30% a month, and that was
   with paydowns above \$20bn reinvested, so it understates the true prepayment pace. Lower rates, faster runoff.
3. **A cap of zero does not mean MBS stops shrinking.** After Aug 2019 and from Dec 2025, paydowns kept running off
   MBS but were reinvested into Treasuries, then bills. Holdings fall; reserves do not. The reserve effect depends
   on where paydowns are reinvested, not on the MBS line alone.
4. **The Fed has wanted out of MBS since 2019** ("primarily Treasury securities in the longer run"), yet in
   practice it has only ever let MBS run off. It has never sold outright, which is what makes active sales the
   tail scenario.
